slides.text: As the city’s top forensic pathologist, I've seen every horror. But the victim on my steel table tonight is different. He was found frozen in a meat locker, perfectly preserved. As I make the Y-incision, I find something impossible. Snagged in his stomach lining is a small, sealed plastic capsule. It hasn’t been digested. I carefully extract it, my scalpel slipping as I realize it contains a tightly rolled piece of notebook paper.

The ink is fresh, written just hours ago, though the victim has been dead for at least a week. My hands tremble as I unroll the tiny note under the blinding surgical lights. It says: 'Dr. Evans. Do not turn around. He is watching you from the observation deck.' I freeze. The observation deck is supposed to be locked and empty at this hour. I can hear the faint squeak of a leather shoe against glass above me.

I slowly reach for my surgical bone saw, keeping my eyes fixed on the dead man's chest. My phone buzzes on the metal tray. It's a text from the night guard: 'Doc, you need to get out of there. I just found the real Dr. Evans dead in the parking lot.' The intercom clicks on. A voice that sounds exactly like mine whispers, 'You did a great job with the incision. Now it's my turn.'
